item.title: 2nd SHOW ADDED - NYTT LAND + MORTIIS + TiR - Southern Ritual - Factory Floor - Sydney - Wed 18th Nov
item.description:
Wed 18 Nov 2026, 8:30 AM – 11:30 AM | Location: The Factory Theatre | SECOND SHOW ADDED!!!
Hardline Media are proud present a dual headline tour, from the Cold Dark Depths of Norway and Siberia featuring MORTIIS and NYTT LAND, with special guest TiR from Turkey, performing their SOUTHERN RITUAL in late November across Australia.
MORTIIS needs no introduction to the Metal world, famous for being the bass player in early EMPEROR, Mortiis has since carved a long and respected career in the Dark Dungeon Synth world for the last 3 + decades. Mortiis has performed in Australia before as a solo one man show, but this time Australia will be treated to something very special... he will be bringing his band with him for the very first time, performing songs from "The Smell Of Rain" album and other volumes of Dystopian Despair. This is a first and not to be missed.
Check out new MORTIIS - "Ghosts Of Europa" https://youtu.be/PQcBobUAwsE
As joint headline and for their first time in Australia, Hardline prouldy present NYTT LAND from Siberia. A phenomenal aural and visual experience.
The band's style has been compared to that of Wardruna and Danheim with added traditional throat singing and handmade traditional instruments such as the Kantele and the Talharpa. Their music has been variously described by reviewers as 'truly authentic feeling', 'dark and mystical' and as 'keeping history alive'. Thematically, their work echoes many stories from Norse mythology and historic texts such as the Poetic Edda. In keeping with this tradition, much of Nytt Land's lyrics are composed and sung in the Old Norse language. See them for the first time in Australia, performing the "Aba Kahn" album and "Siberian Era" started on "Ritual".
Witness NYTT LAND - "U-Gra" https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TmR-pO6JT60
As National support, Hardline welcome TiR. Originally hailing from Turkey, TiR are a Dungeon Synth Folk project helmed by multi-instrumentalist and composer Oytun Bektas. For over a decade, TiR has carved a distinct artistic path where ancient melancholy and pastoral introspection merge into a cinematic soundscape that bridges the past and the universal.
Watch TiR - "Vengeance" www.youtube.com/watch?v=1PpEupF8aM4
This triple bill is surely not to be missed, for all fans of Dark, Ambient, Pagan Folk music, even Black Metal and all fans of quality music, come and witness the aural and visual magnificence of MORTIIS + NYTT LAND + TiR. You will not be disappointed, so get your tickets early as they are expected to go fast!
DO NOT MISS THESE SHOWS!

UK psychedelic heavyweights Uncle Acid & The Deadbeats will return to Australia this December, bringing their dark, hypnotic live show to stages across the country.
The brainchild of Kevin Starrs, Uncle Acid & The Deadbeats have spent over a decade carving out a singular space within the global heavy music landscape. Since emerging in 2009 from the depths of the British underground, the band have built a reputation for their unmistakable fusion of warped psychedelic pop, downer blues and doom-metal intensity.
Too bold and idiosyncratic to be easily defined, Uncle Acid’s sound is steeped in haunting melodies, layered vocal harmonies and eerie, cinematic arrangements, offset by crushing riffs and a persistent sense of unease. It’s a sonic world that feels both deeply nostalgic and completely otherworldly.

2027 will bring pure ecstasy for Australian 𝗕𝗘𝗔𝗥𝗧𝗢𝗢𝗧𝗛 fans, with the prolific rockers today announcing their biggest Australian headline tour ever next January, joined by special guests 𝗙𝗜𝗧 𝗙𝗢𝗥 𝗔 𝗞𝗜𝗡𝗚 and 𝗩𝗢𝗟𝗨𝗠𝗘𝗦.
Kicking off in Adelaide on Tuesday 26 January next year, 𝗕𝗘𝗔𝗥𝗧𝗢𝗢𝗧𝗛 will head to Melbourne and Sydney before closing out proceedings on Sunday 31 January in Brisbane.
𝗕𝗘𝗔𝗥𝗧𝗢𝗢𝗧𝗛 has also announced that their new album, 𝗣𝘂𝗿𝗲 𝗘𝗰𝘀𝘁𝗮𝘀𝘆, will be released on August 28 via their new label home, Fearless Records. Marking the band’s sixth album and first release with the label, 𝗣𝘂𝗿𝗲 𝗘𝗰𝘀𝘁𝗮𝘀𝘆 finds frontman 𝗖𝗮𝗹𝗲𝗯 𝗦𝗵𝗼𝗺𝗼 pushing 𝗕𝗘𝗔𝗥𝗧𝗢𝗢𝗧𝗛 further than ever before across 11 massive tracks that channel both the chaos and clarity of hard-won personal growth.
The band has dropped the album’s opening title-track where 𝗦𝗵𝗼𝗺𝗼 lays everything bare from the first note. It’s a raw, disorienting entry point - where extremes of emotion blur together - setting the tone for an album built on confronting every high and low without flinching. “Song one is always a crucial part of an album to me. It’s gotta lock you into the vibe out of the gate,” says 𝗦𝗵𝗼𝗺𝗼. “‘Pure Ecstasy’ was birthed in a studio with Misha Mansoor, ridiculous loudspeakers, and the dumbest heaviest chugs we could chug. Once it was brought home and expanded on with Jordan Fish, there was no question it was the album opener. Play loud and kick ass.” Following the chart-dominating success of 2023’s 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗦𝘂𝗿𝗳𝗮𝗰𝗲 - which debuted at No.1 on Billboard’s Alternative and Hard Music charts and produced the No.1 rock radio hits 𝘮𝘪𝘨𝘩𝘵 𝘭𝘰𝘷𝘦 𝘮𝘺𝘴𝘦𝘭𝘧 and 𝘪 𝘸𝘢𝘴 𝘢𝘭𝘪𝘷𝘦 - 𝗕𝗘𝗔𝗥𝗧𝗢𝗢𝗧𝗛 entered a new creative and commercial stratosphere. 𝗣𝘂𝗿𝗲 𝗘𝗰𝘀𝘁𝗮𝘀𝘆 builds on that momentum while expanding the band into even more ambitious territory, capturing 𝗦𝗵𝗼𝗺𝗼 reckoning with both the darkest and brightest parts of himself in real time.
The album’s first single 𝗙𝗿𝗲𝗲, released earlier this year, introduced this next chapter of 𝗕𝗘𝗔𝗥𝗧𝗢𝗢𝗧𝗛 with towering hooks and radical self-examination. 𝗦𝗵𝗼𝗺𝗼 cites the song as “the most honest depiction of my soul I will most likely ever make.”
That honesty has always been the foundation of 𝗕𝗘𝗔𝗥𝗧𝗢𝗢𝗧𝗛. Since emerging from 𝗦𝗵𝗼𝗺𝗼’𝘀 Ohio basement in 2013, the band has transformed anxiety, depression, anger, and self-destruction into cathartic modern rock anthems that resonate with millions worldwide. From the gold-certified 𝘩𝘢𝘵𝘦𝘥 and platinum 𝘪𝘯 𝘣𝘦𝘵𝘸𝘦𝘦𝘯 to over 1.3 billion streams globally, sold-out tours, and a recent run supporting Bad Omens on their arena tour, 𝗕𝗘𝗔𝗥𝗧𝗢𝗢𝗧𝗛’𝘀 rise has mirrored the growing mainstream dominance of modern heavy music itself.
But 𝗣𝘂𝗿𝗲 𝗘𝗰𝘀𝘁𝗮𝘀𝘆 represents something different. Bigger and more collaborative than any previous 𝗕𝗘𝗔𝗥𝗧𝗢𝗢𝗧𝗛 album, the record finds 𝗦𝗵𝗼𝗺𝗼 stretching himself toward a new level of vulnerability - and for the first time he didn’t do it alone. Early songwriting contributions from Skyler Accord (Issues, Twenty One Pilots, Bilmuri) helped shape early tracks. Meanwhile, working alongside Fish (Bring Me The Horizon, Poppy, Architects) cracked Caleb fully open, pushing a rawer examination than ever before. The collaborative spirit continued throughout the recording process as well: bassist Oshie Bichar, guitarists Zach Huston and Will Deely, and drummer Connor Denis - who have evolved into a formidable live unit around 𝗦𝗵𝗼𝗺𝗼 — all played larger roles than ever before. 𝗣𝘂𝗿𝗲 𝗘𝗰𝘀𝘁𝗮𝘀𝘆 also marks the first 𝗕𝗘𝗔𝗥𝗧𝗢𝗢𝗧𝗛 album where 𝗦𝗵𝗼𝗺𝗼 did not perform every instrument himself, with Denis performing drums across the record during sessions at NRG Recording Studios.
For years, 𝗕𝗘𝗔𝗥𝗧𝗢𝗢𝗧𝗛 turned pain into anthems shouted back at the world. 𝗣𝘂𝗿𝗲 𝗘𝗰𝘀𝘁𝗮𝘀𝘆 captures what happens on the other side of that fight: not perfection or peace, but the possibility of freedom.
Unsurprisingly, 𝗕𝗘𝗔𝗥𝗧𝗢𝗢𝗧𝗛'𝘀 live shows are as cathartic and immersive as the band's beloved back catalogue, routinely praised as one of the top-tier modern bands on the scene, complete with intensity, theatrical flourishes, a healthy balance of new and classic favourites, and a personal connection that transcends barriers and expectations. Helmed by 𝗦𝗵𝗼𝗺𝗼'𝘀 raw and passionate stylings, 𝗕𝗘𝗔𝗥𝗧𝗢𝗢𝗧𝗛'𝘀 return to Australia in 2027 will build on the band's previous live adventures down under, with their most recent co-headline run with Pierce The Veil in 2023 resoundingly praised.
Erupting out of Texas in 2011, 𝗙𝗜𝗧 𝗙𝗢𝗥 𝗔 𝗞𝗜𝗡𝗚 swiftly carved out a name for themselves with a blistering style rooted in metal and hardcore, while also balancing out their raucous tendencies with plenty of hypnotic hooks and searing honesty for good measure. Releasing their breakout album in 2013, 𝗖𝗿𝗲𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻/𝗗𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗿𝘂𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 which debuted at #6 on the Hard Rock Chart, 𝗙𝗜𝗧 𝗙𝗢𝗥 𝗔 𝗞𝗜𝗡𝗚 have gone on to command multiple Top 5 debuts on the Billboard Charts, generate millions of streams, including fan-favourite tracks like 𝘸𝘩𝘦𝘯 𝘦𝘷𝘦𝘳𝘺𝘵𝘩𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘮𝘦𝘢𝘯𝘴 𝘯𝘰𝘵𝘩𝘪𝘯𝘨, 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘱𝘳𝘪𝘤𝘦 𝘰𝘧 𝘢𝘨𝘰𝘯𝘺 and 𝘣𝘳𝘦𝘢𝘬𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘮𝘪𝘳𝘳𝘰𝘳, and have extensively toured the globe with Killswitch Engage, Motionless In White, I Prevail, Parkway Drive, The Devil Wears Prada and The Plot In You. Most recently the group released their eighth studio album, 2025's 𝗟𝗼𝗻𝗲𝗹𝘆 𝗚𝗼𝗱 scored critical acclaim for its balance of heavy breakdowns, atmospheric elements, and emotionally driven songwriting.
15 years into their career, 𝗩𝗢𝗟𝗨𝗠𝗘𝗦 have weathered ups, downs, time, trends, and everything else life could throw at them only to come out stronger on the other side. With over 167 million streams in the United States alone, widespread acclaim, and sold-out shows, they loudly carved out their own corner of heavy music with an inimitable hybrid of head-crushing polyrhythmic prog-spiked metal, hardcore spirit, and unbridled attitude. They have assuredly levelled up over the course of albums such as 𝗩𝗶𝗮 [2011], 𝗡𝗼 𝗦𝗹𝗲𝗲𝗽 [2014], 𝗗𝗶𝗳𝗳𝗲𝗿𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗔𝗻𝗶𝗺𝗮𝗹𝘀 [2017], and 𝗛𝗮𝗽𝗽𝗶𝗲𝗿? [2021] and fifth release, 𝗠𝗶𝗿𝗿𝗼𝗿 𝗧𝗼𝘂𝗰𝗵 released in 2025 via Fearless Records. They've shared stages with everyone from Ice Nine Kills and Born of Osiris to Dance Gavin Dance and Counterparts. The Los Angeles group continues to fortify a full-on sensory assault with thick riffing, chilling soundscapes, and the venomous bite of its incomparable two-headed vocal hydra.
Start your 2027 off revelling in wall-to-wall ecstasy when 𝗕𝗘𝗔𝗥𝗧𝗢𝗢𝗧𝗛 make their triumphant return with 𝗙𝗜𝗧 𝗙𝗢𝗥 𝗔 𝗞𝗜𝗡𝗚 and 𝗩𝗢𝗟𝗨𝗠𝗘𝗦, tickets will absolutely not last long!

Fri 5 Feb 2027, 8:00 AM – 12:00 PM | Location: Manning Bar | DEICIDE ARE COMING TO AUSTRALIA — AND THEY’RE BRINGING HELL WITH THEM!
Death Metal’s Most Uncompromising Force Returns Down Under for the First Time Since 2006!
DEICIDE are back!
After more than 20 years away from Australian stages, one of the most notorious, influential and downright punishing bands in the history of death metal will finally return to Australia in January and February 2027.
The Tampa, Florida death metal institution will unleash their assault across Adelaide, Brisbane, Canberra, Melbourne and Sydney, delivering a long-overdue dose of the brutality that has made DEICIDE one of the biggest names the genre has ever produced.
Formed in Tampa in 1987 by bassist/vocalist Glen Benton and drummer/composer Steve Asheim, DEICIDE didn't just become part of the death metal movement — they helped define it.
When their self-titled debut detonated in 1990, the band's blueprint was already brutally clear: savage riffs, relentless drumming, demonic intensity and absolutely zero interest in compromise. Then came Legion in 1992, a landmark record that propelled DEICIDE into the international metal spotlight and cemented their place among death metal's elite.
Their impact has been enormous. DEICIDE are credited as the second-best-selling death metal band of the SoundScan era, while their first two albums became major commercial benchmarks for extreme metal. By November 2003, Deicide and Legion ranked second and third respectively among the best-selling death metal albums of the SoundScan era.
More than three decades later, the band has built a formidable catalogue spanning twelve studio albums, one live album, two compilation albums and two live DVDs. But statistics only tell part of the story.
DEICIDE's legacy has been forged in blood, volume and sheer sonic violence. Their music has remained relentlessly hostile, uncompromising and unapologetically extreme through changing trends, musical fashions and generations of metal bands. Now the wait is over.
After more than 20 years, DEICIDE are finally coming back Down Under.
For Australian fans who have been waiting since 2006, DEICIDE will once again bring their blasphemous, skull-crushing death metal to our shores.

Pack your bags Australia, Camp Screamo is headed our way in 2027! Hot off selling out their Camp Screamo co-headline run across North America, Missouri stalwarts STORY OF THE YEAR and Canadian legends SILVERSTEIN will bring this huge tour down under next February, joined by special guests POINT NORTH (USA).
Opening in Melbourne on Friday 5 February, STORY OF THE YEAR and SILVERSTEIN will head through Sydney, Adelaide and Fremantle, before closing out in Brisbane on Friday 12 February.
"The Camp Screamo Tour with our old friends, Silverstein, has been so sick that we HAD TO take it to one of our favorite places on Earth for the third leg. See you in February, Australia!" - Story Of The Year
"Australia has been a favourite touring destination of ours for over 20 years! We are very excited to bring Camp Screamo down under, including our full Production and a killer line-up of bands (our best pals Story of the Year and Point North). We are going to give Australians the show they deserve, and can’t wait for this tour to kick off. See you there!" - Silverstein
Few records helped build the post hardcore scene more than STORY OF THE YEAR's 2003 debut album Page Avenue. An evergreen favourite, a masterpiece of the genre, and also one of the first of its kind to sell one million copies, Page Avenue ultimately set the scene for STORY OF THE YEAR's 30+ year career, with the band since going on to release seven studio albums to date against ongoing commercial success and global adoration.
Most recently releasing their latest studio album A.R.S.O.N. earlier this year, STORY OF THE YEAR once again showcased their signature brand of intense, passionate and confessional compositions that simultaneously inspire and empower, with KERRANG! noting of the record, "seven albums in, Story Of The Year are still breaking new ground with the energy of a band that is just getting started. Now that’s a story worth telling". And the band's back catalogue is equally stacked, with anthems like Until the Day I Die, Anthem of Our Dying Day and And the Hero Will Drown joining forces with other earlier favourites to define the early 2000s post hardcore explosion, championing triumph over adversity in the process.
From teenagers working in a St. Louis pizza shop into international headliners, STORY OF THE YEAR have previously performed alongside the likes of Linkin Park, My Chemical Romance, Deftones and The Used. Most recently, the group whipped across Australia in 2024 to celebrate the 20th anniversary of their debut full-length Page Avenue, with The Rockpit enthusing of their Melbourne performance: "Story of the Year were as energetic and tight as ever, blowing everyone away with their skill and dedication to not only their craft, but their fans too."
For over 25 years, Ontario, Canada-bred rockers SILVERSTEIN have remained at the top of the emo and post hardcore scenes. Innovative and inspiring at every turn, the group's landmark moment arrived in 2005 with the release of their sophomore album Discovering the Waterfront, garnering a Juno Award for New Group of the Year, peaking at #34 on the Billboard 200 charts and introducing the world to iconic singles like Smile in Your Sleep.
A band at the forefront of the mid-2000s emo and screamo explosion, SILVERSTEIN have since sold over one million records worldwide, generated over 500 million streams, and continue to cement their reputation as ambitious yet intelligent creatives, releasing concept albums like 2009's A Shipwreck in the Sand and 2013's This Is How the Wind Shifts, and, more recently, their Juno Award-nominated 2020 album A Beautiful Place to Drown and their 2025 dual album, Antibloom and Pink Moon. Helmed by frontman Shane Told, who was voted among the Five Best Post-Hardcore Vocalists by Alternative Press readers, songs like My Heroine, Smile In Your Sleep, The Afterglow and Infinite are ingrained in the scene's DNA.
Performing across the globe to packed crowds singing and screaming along with every word, SILVERSTEIN have shared stages over the years with everyone from Simple Plan through to Rise Against, Good Charlotte and Pierce The Veil. Performing down under in 2025 for their 25th anniversary, SILVERSTEIN's unforgettable set in Brisbane had Scenestr praising: "still loud, still raw, still punching holes in the dark, Silverstein at 25 are not limping toward legacy but tearing through it sideways, bloodied and burning. This ain't a victory lap. It's a demolition."
Forming in 2017, Los Angeles, California rockers POINT NORTH unleashed their debut full-length Brand New Vision in 2020, praised for its genre-fluid style and tantalising hues of alt rock, pop punk, hip hop, R&B and electronic pop. From there, POINT NORTH released their sophomore album Prepare For Despair in 2023, and have also previously collaborated with nothing, nowhere., Kellin Quinn from Sleeping With Sirens, FEVER 333 and many more. With an electrifying live set to accompany their immersive creations, POINT NORTH have toured alongside From Ashes To New, Falling In Reverse, Set It Off and DON BROCO, and ticked off their debut Australian performances in 2025 supporting Ocean Sleeper.
Uniting two enduring legends of the scene for career-spanning sets and unforgettable moments from start to finish, don't miss STORY OF THE YEAR and SILVERSTEIN joining forces down under in 2027: Camp Screamo is not to be missed!

Swedish metalcore phenomenon Thrown today announce their return to Australia after selling out their entire February 2025 headline tour and will be back this February. Marking Thrown's biggest Australian headline tour to date they'll be joined by special guests Connecticut's Boundaries, Pittsburgh's 156/Silence and opening proceedings will be Australia's own Volatile Ways.
Since emerging from Stockholm, Thrown have established themselves as one of the fastest-rising forces in modern heavy music. Extensive touring alongside acts including Knocked Loose, Counterparts, Fit For A King, While She Sleeps, Wage War and many more has cemented their reputation as one of metalcore's most explosive live bands. Today, thrown continue their meteoric rise with well over one million monthly Spotify listeners and hundreds of millions of streams worldwide.
Thrown recently released "critic," a ferocious new single out now via Arising Empire. Sharp-tongued, crushingly heavy and unapologetically confrontational, the track takes aim at self-appointed tastemakers, performative outrage and the endless cycle of online commentary, proving once again that thrown thrive where others merely make noise. Fuelled by venomous vocals, bone-crushing grooves and explosive breakdowns, "critic" is a ruthless response to a culture obsessed with opinions, metrics and manufactured controversy.
Boundaries are coming in hot, off the heels of their new album Yearning: the unbeautiful after. Recorded with producer Drew Fulk (Knocked Loose, Fit For A King), Yearning: the unbeautiful after captures Boundaries at their most punishing, deliberate, and focused. The 14-track album features guest appearances from The Plot In You’s Landon Tewers (“Crowned and crucified”) and Make Them Suffer (“Torn wide open”). With Boundaries recent visit to Australia supporting The Plot In You on a fully sold out tour, fans know what to expect to from the Connecticut metalcore group.
156/Silence are finally making their debut to our shores where they'll bring their intense, foreboding, and haunting music. Their songs are cinematic, blending brutality with intellect. They draw on real and imagined terror, all woven into melody and power. The band will release their sixth studio album, From A Distance, on September 4, 2026, through Pure Noise Records.
Rounding out the bill will be Newcastle's Volatile Ways with their hard mosh death core made by hardcore kids. With unmatched energy that radiates through their playful disposition at live shows and honouring femininity, the multifaceted four-piece manage to bring brutality to the forefront; having shared stages with The Acacia Strain, Fit For An Autopsy, Bodysnatcher, Kublai Khan, Thrown, Dying Wish and Speed among others.

Forming in 2012, 𝗗𝗔𝗬𝗦𝗘𝗘𝗞𝗘𝗥 have relentlessly adhered to a pursuit of truth, passion, innovation and vulnerability, announcing themselves to the world. With the release of their cinematic sixth studio album, 𝗖𝗿𝗲𝗮𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲 𝗜𝗻 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗕𝗹𝗮𝗰𝗸 𝗡𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁. Down under, the band's previous 2024 debut Australian headline tour was completely sold out, and their most recent performances as part of Good Things Festival in 2025.
